claim: Île de Bendor is a 7-10 minute boat ride from Bandol port and reopened in 2026 after 5 years of work as a Zannier-managed destination with three hotels, restaurants, bars and a new wellness area.
quote: A small, (almost) lost paradise located about ten minutes by boat from Bandol, the island of Bendor is a feast for the senses. After 5 years of work, Bendor, a place of reflection, passion and love, is accessible again.

claim: The Bendor shuttle from Bandol port runs May to November 2026, every 30 minutes from 10am to 11:30pm, with a 7-minute crossing and online-only ticketing.
quote: The shuttle to Bendor runs from May 1 to November 1, 2026... departing from Bandol port every 30 minutes... The crossing takes precisely 7 minutes... No physical ticket office is available - reservations must be made online.

claim: Bandol is a wine-anchored port town: the AOC dates to 1941, the vines enjoy 3000 hours of sunshine and the powerful Mourvèdre-based reds and pale-salmon rosés define its character.
quote: Bandol was built around its wines... the vineyard was one of the first to benefit from the AOC appellation in 1941... 3000 hours of sunshine per year... knew how to tame a difficult vine plant: the Mourvèdre. This grape gives wines of great quality.

claim: Sanary-sur-Mer's Wednesday market runs 8am-1pm year-round along the port under plane trees, gathers 300+ vendors and was voted the most beautiful market in France by TF1 viewers in 2018.
quote: Every Wednesday, all year round from 8 AM to 1 PM, along the port and under the plane trees on the Allées d'Estienne d'Orves... This market gathers more than 300 vendors... In 2018, the large weekly market of Sanary was voted the most beautiful market in France by the viewers of the television channel TF1.

claim: La Ciotat's Eden Théâtre is the oldest purpose-built cinema in operation per Guinness World Records (entered 2021); it opened in 1889, hosted the first paying Lumière screening in 1899 and was reopened in 2013 after restoration.
quote: the oldest cinema in the world... oldest purpose-built cinema in operation... In 1895, it was the site of the first public showing of a film, 'Arrivé d'un Train à La Ciotat'... reopened and has again become a popular cinema.

claim: La Ciotat presents itself as the 'true cradle of cinema': Louis Lumière perfected the cinematograph there in summer 1895 and the first paying screening took place at the Eden Théâtre on 21 March 1899.
quote: During the summer of 1895, Louis Lumière perfected the cinematograph and began shooting some thirty films among the first in the history of cinema... The first paying cinema screening took place on 21 March 1899 at the Éden Théâtre, making La Ciotat the true cradle of cinema.

claim: Cassis's calling card is its Calanques and port-side beaches: En Vau is the most spectacular with steep white cliffs, Port Pin the most intimate with Aleppo pines, and Cap Canaille looms over Bestouan beach.
quote: The most famous and spectacular of the Calanques is picture-postcard beautiful... The smallest and most intimate of the three Calanques boasts a profusion of Aleppo pines that grow directly out of the rock face... In skyline, Cape Canaille in majesty...

claim: Boat tours of the Calanques depart from Cassis port year-round in 3, 5, 8 or 9-calanque circuits run by the GIE des Bateliers Cassidiens fleet.
quote: Between Cassis and Marseille, you can choose tours of 3, 5, 8 or 9 Calanques (creeks). The tour of the Calanques operates all year round, every day.

claim: Cap Canaille between Cassis and La Ciotat is the highest sea cliff in Europe at 399 m, accessed via the D141 Route des Crêtes ridge road.
quote: The Cap Canaille, with an altitude of 399 meters, is the highest point of the massif and the highest sea cliff in Europe.

claim: Saint-Cyr-sur-Mer's signature curiosity is an authentic golden cast-iron scale replica of New York's Statue of Liberty, displayed at Place Portalis with Bartholdi's signature on the pedestal, inaugurated 1913.
quote: Located in Place Portalis, the city is very proud to be in possession of an authentic replica of the New York City's Statue of Liberty in scale model.

claim: Les Lecques at Saint-Cyr-sur-Mer is a 2 km family sand beach lined by the 'Pink Promenade', with water-sports rentals, private beaches and easy parking.
quote: Les Lecques beach is a large family beach with fine sand with a landscaped promenade, known as the Pink Promenade, featuring a 2 km stretch of sand and postcard views.

claim: Six-Fours' Île des Embiez, reached in ~10 min by boat from Le Brusc, is a car-free Paul Ricard island concentrating 90% of regional flora and fauna and is part of the European Natura 2000 network.
quote: An unspoilt jewel in the Mediterranean, the Paul Ricard Islands are a veritable ode to nature... 90% of the fauna and flora of our beautiful region found here... Protected from concrete, car traffic on the island is very limited... can be reached in just 10 minutes by taking a boat.

claim: Driving distances from Le Castellet are short: ~11 km/17 min to Bandol, ~26 km/22 min to Cassis, ~32 km Bandol-Cassis as a coastal loop.
quote: Cassis to Le Castellet: The drive takes 22 minutes and the distance is 25.7 kilometers. Bandol to Le Castellet: approximately 11 km and takes approximately 17 minutes.
